hypothesis: Verified one-hop regulatory relationships can safely augment the existing dense-plus-BM25 retrieval path for relationship questions without replacing extraction, OCR, VLM, chunking, embedding, or baseline fallback behavior.

changed: deterministic French, Arabic, and English relationship routing
graph evidence conversion to source-linked LangChain documents
bounded union and reranking in the existing chat retrieval path
optional Neo4j runtime lifecycle and observable graph trace

conclusion: Keep the minimal relationship-aware runtime integration. It reuses the existing retrieval and verified graph-ingestion seams and follows graph relationships only when a relationship question and regulatory seed justify expansion.
limitations: The runtime can retrieve only relationships already verified and persisted in Neo4j.
The persistent graph currently contains three DECLARES_CHANGE relationships and no DECLARES_REFERENCE relationships; reference traversal was verified only in the disposable live fixture.
Traversal is deliberately limited to one hop, five ordinary-retrieval seeds, and ten evidence records.
The routing rules are deterministic and conservative, so unusual relationship wording may remain on the ordinary retrieval path.
The graph trace is internal runtime observability and is not exposed in the public response model.
No answer-quality benchmark or accuracy claim was made; provisional and final evaluation sets remained unopened.
recommendation: Use the existing verified per-document relationship-ingestion seam to populate additional reviewed relationships as documents arrive, then run a bounded gold-blind answer-quality evaluation before production promotion.
